bullets.title: Fed's Warsh adopts 'purposeful obfuscation' — rate volatility rising, hike risk building
bullets.body: New Fed Chair Warsh is deliberately minimizing forward guidance, with markets interpreting the lack of pushback as tacit acceptance of current pricing. Morgan Stanley recommends SOFR curve flatteners and tactically underweight mortgages; half of Fed governors are leaning toward a hike. JPM flags core PCE must average ~0.21%/month to avoid tightening risk, and the US economic surprise index is at its highest since 2023.

bullets.title: Market in late-cycle: narrow AI leadership, record inflows, extreme positioning
bullets.body: AI names represent ~39% of S&P 500 weighting approaching historical extremes; record $119.2B weekly inflow to US stocks with tech annualizing $154B in 2026. Systematic flows are asymmetric: flat market sees $13B buy but a down market triggers $95B in selling. Hedge fund gross leverage is at the 100th percentile, and median short % across the Russell 3000 is the highest since at least 2010. ~$8.3T options expiration and quarter-end pension rebalancing likely to drive near-term volatility.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle underpriced: MU/SNDK locked into multi-year AI contracts at 9x forward
bullets.body: MS and Klein's desk see DRAM ASPs +45% and NAND ASPs +50% in FY27, with MU FY27 EPS raised to $21.31; stock trades at just 9x forward despite multiyear tightness. SNDK has locked >1/3 of FY27 bits under 3–5 year NBM agreements as cloud becomes its largest end-market. Separately, MU announced a strategic supply and investment agreement with Anthropic. Semis broadly are up ~70% in Q2 with order visibility extending 2–3 years.

bullets.title: GOOGL under pressure: DeepMind talent exodus to Anthropic/OpenAI, stock -2.4% pre-market
bullets.body: Nobel laureate John Jumper (AlphaFold co-creator) is leaving Google DeepMind for Anthropic; Noam Shazeer previously defected to OpenAI. GOOGL was also struggling to sell AI coding tools per Citi's TMT desk, and Chinese AI models are overtaking US counterparts in token consumption. GOOGL opened down ~2.45%.

bullets.title: AMZN and GOOGL escalating custom-silicon threat to NVDA; AVGO also gaining share
bullets.body: AMZN is in talks to sell Trainium chips to third-party data centers (Trainium3 largely sold out, Trainium4 expected next year); GOOGL is moving from TPU cloud provider to direct external chip sales with financing and cloud partnerships. AVGO faces potential share loss to Mediatek at GOOG on TPUv9 (Triggerfish), though at 30% higher ASPs. NVDA retains strong positioning but faces more direct competition than prior narratives suggested.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure bottleneck shifting from GPUs to memory, edge hardware, and power
bullets.body: Mac mini/Studio scarcity signals edge AI demand outpacing supply; Apple Silicon's unified memory makes these devices ideal for local inference and agentic workflows. The thesis: better model efficiency paradoxically increases total compute demand (Jevons Paradox), and physical constraints in memory fabs, packaging, and power cannot respond as fast as software advances. Until Apple is oversupplied with high-memory local AI machines, the infrastructure cycle is not broadly oversupplied.

bullets.title: MSFT pivots AI strategy to model commoditization and multi-vendor inference; signs 2.67 GW power deal
bullets.body: MSFT CEO Nadella is repositioning around lower-cost inference, orchestration, and enterprise control rather than frontier-model dependency — including exploring hosting DeepSeek despite the OpenAI partnership. Separately, MSFT signed a 20-year, 2.67 GW gas power deal (Project Kilby) with Chevron near Pecos, TX, with first power by 2028 at mid-teen returns.

bullets.title: ACN negative bookings drag entire IT Services sector; buyside avoiding the group
bullets.body: Accenture posted negative bookings growth well below bearish expectations, sending IT Services peers lower (INFY reportedly down 10–18%). The buyside is broadly avoiding the sector on structural headwinds from AI displacing traditional consulting and services spend. ACN is down ~59% from its 52-week high.

bullets.title: AMZN Prime Day signals consumer strain: spending +9% y/y but shifting to groceries and basics
bullets.body: Prime Day spending is expected to reach $26.3B (+9% y/y), but the mix has shifted toward groceries, back-to-school, and basics rather than discretionary items — a consumer stress signal. Gas below $4/gallon supports the overall environment, but the composition of spending is a concern.

bullets.title: Chinese AI models gaining rapidly; DeepSeek hits #1 on Ramp's June trending software index
bullets.body: Chinese AI models (DeepSeek V4 Flash, MiniMax M3, Hy3) are showing the fastest growth on OpenRouter, and DeepSeek attained #1 position in Ramp's June 2026 trending software vendors index for the first time. Citi notes Chinese AI models are overtaking US counterparts in token consumption, adding pricing pressure on US AI vendors.

bullets.title: Fox/Roku $22B deal, Salesforce/Fin $3.6B, Accenture $4.2B cybersecurity acquisitions headline M&A week
bullets.body: Fox Corporation is acquiring Roku for $160/share in cash and stock (~$22B EV). Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Fin for ~$3.6B. Accenture announced acquisitions of runZero, NetRise, and a majority stake in Dragos at a combined ~$4.175B. Netflix is reportedly in contract to acquire Radford Studio Center for ~$400M.

bullets.title: DLR announces $1.61B in transactions: 2GW Kansas City site, Teraco stake increase, Columbia Capital
bullets.body: Digital Realty's three deals include a ~$475M 1,440-acre Kansas City site (600MW by 2028, scaling to 2GW), a ~$650M increase in Teraco ownership to 77% (implied 24x TTM FFO vs DLR's 28x — accretive), and a ~$485M acquisition of Columbia Capital ($9B AUM AI infrastructure platform). Funded via 6.3M share issuance at $197.54 plus ~$365M cash; expected to be slightly accretive in 2026 and significantly more accretive over time.

bullets.title: FERC and Texas advancing data center grid interconnection; power/labor emerging as key constraints
bullets.body: FERC's decision pushes PJM toward faster data center interconnection rules and co-location mechanisms. Texas is advancing batch approval for data center grid connections with 35 GW baseload plus 65 GW under study in 'Batch Zero.' Labor constraints are emerging alongside power as a binding constraint for natural gas plant engineering and construction.

bullets.title: Mag-7 down YTD while rest of S&P +20%; Q2 earnings breadth expanding with 22% EPS growth expected
bullets.body: Mag-7 stocks are down YTD while the broader S&P 500 ex-Mag-7 is up ~20%, with the rally broadening materially. Q2 earnings growth is expected at 22.0% (7th consecutive quarter of double-digit EPS growth), with Tech sector projected at 54.8% EPS growth. All 11 S&P sectors are expected to deliver positive revenue growth.

bullets.title: JPM: US headline CPI seen at 3.9%, core PCE at 3.4% through July 2026 — above Fed target
bullets.body: JPMorgan's monthly inflation forecast has US headline CPI at 3.9% y/y and core CPI at 2.8% y/y through July 2026; core PCE is projected at 3.4% y/y. Nine FOMC members anticipate rate hikes in 2026 per the latest dots, keeping the Fed on a hawkish tilt.

bullets.title: INTC +10% on AAPL foundry partnership; advanced packaging seen gaining 10-15% market share
bullets.body: Intel surged ~10% on news of an Apple partnership for US foundry construction. Mizuho raised INTC PT to $135 from $128 seeing potential for 10-15% advanced packaging market share; INTC's EMIB technology is reportedly lower cost than TSMC CoWoS-L. Separately, INTC hired the former SK Hynix CEO for its foundry business, a positive signal for customer wins.

bullets.title: 52-week high/low divergence sharp: semis surging (SNDK +4787%, MU +872%) while SaaS/IT lag (ACN -59%, INTU -65%)
bullets.body: Electronic Technology shows 38 stocks at 52-week highs vs 1 at lows, while Technology Services shows 14 highs but 27 lows. SNDK is up 4787% on a 52-week basis, MU +872%, INTC +542%, ALAB +333%, AMD +342%. On the losing side, ACN is down 59%, INTU down 65%, CHTR down 66%, CRM down 41% from their 52-week highs — a stark sector bifurcation.

bullets.title: Robinhood agentic trading hits 50K users in ~3 weeks; fintech regulation intensifying around prediction markets
bullets.body: Robinhood's agentic trading product launched ~3 weeks ago and already has 50K+ customers trading millions daily; the company also cut ~10% of its workforce. On the regulatory front, the CFTC sued New Mexico to assert authority over prediction markets, CME sued CFTC over Kalshi perps approval, and federal stablecoin regulation is advancing with FDIC/Fed treating issuers as Bank Secrecy Act institutions.

bullets.title: Oil down ~2% on Iran diplomatic progress; WTI ~$74.50 with potential $80-90 range if talks stall
bullets.body: WTI fell ~1.74% to $74.53 pre-market on progress in Iran-US negotiations around sanctions waivers and Strait of Hormuz passage. Brent declined ~2.5% to below $79/barrel. JPM notes a potential $80–90 WTI range if geopolitical stability remains elusive.

bullets.title: Euro area consumer confidence improving but still 1.6 std devs below average; Q2 spending nowcast turns positive
bullets.body: Euro area consumer confidence rose 1.3pts in June, broadly in-line with expectations, with JPMorgan's Q2 household spending nowcast revised to +0.1–0.4% annualized from a prior -0.5% contraction. Improvement is driven by moderating fuel prices and labor market resilience, though sentiment remains depressed at ~1.6 standard deviations below historical average.
